title: Wait for pending checks before merging; treat rule-violation refusal as
summary: The drain asked GitHub to merge while a non-required check run was still in progress, was refused with 'Repository rule violations', and stopped the run. The change makes check classification report pending while any check run on the head is queued or in progress, and makes a rule-violation merge refusal a wait: the drain reports the job as waiting to merge and moves to the next job. The audience is the person running the drain.

defaults_applied.how: New gh and drain tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria run tests showing pending classification, no merge call, and the drain continuing.
Fixes both the premature merge request (pending runs ignored) and the drain's handling of the refusal.
One focused change across gh and drain.
Independent verifier runs the named tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs (classify_checks decides only on the required CI_AGGREGATE_JOB run, so an in-progress optional run reads Green); crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs (wait_for_checks polls check_report until not Pending); crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs (land_pr calls host.merge only when merge_via_rest && checks == Green, and a merge error propagates as Err); crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (PrLander::land maps Err to Landing::NotLanded, which the drain counts as a failed landing). Property is measured directly via classify_checks output and via the Landing value PrLander returns.
No record or data file under crates/ is added, so records validation (check_record_file, AnyRecord) is not touched.

Rule-violation detection matches the error text 'Repository rule violations' from the host merge call; it is converted into a pending report (merge not confirmed) in land_pr, and PrLander/drain reports a waiting-to-merge outcome instead of a failure. The exact enum shape (a new Landing variant or a flag on PrReport) is the producer's choice, consistent with how the drain handles other not-landed outcomes.
Check runs with status queued or in_progress count as pending; completed runs with failure conclusions stay: required failure is Red, optional failure is a note only.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A gh test in crates/athena-core/src/gh/tests.rs: check runs with the required CI_AGGREGATE_JOB completed green plus another check run in_progress classify as Checks::Pending, and a land_pr run against the fake host makes no merge call (merge_requested false). Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.

A classify test shows a failed optional check run (completed, failure) with the required check green is still Green with a note, and a failed required check is Red. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.

A gh test: when the fake host's merge returns an error containing 'Repository rule violations' while checks are not all complete, land_pr returns a pending/waiting result rather than Err. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.

A drain test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: a merge refused for rule violations is reported as waiting to merge (not a failed landing), the run does not stop, and the next job is worked. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing waiting on pending check runs and treating a rule-violation merge refusal as waiting.
`cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
Doc comments on classify_checks and wait_for_checks are updated to state that any queued or in-progress check run makes the verdict pending.

out_of_scope: Reading required checks from branch protection instead of the fixed CI_AGGREGATE_JOB name.
Changing the re-run logic for red required checks.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows.
departures: Spans gh classification, landing flow and drain outcome types, so slightly above the reference cost.
urgent_reason: It cuts failed landings and stopped drain runs that waste time and force a manual 'athena land --pr' retry.
hard_reason: It changes the landing gate (when a merge is requested) and the drain's handling of a refused merge, which can hold or stop work.
